_about: Fracture data for the fracture engine (tools/fracture_engine.py). One row per AO/OTA 2018 code. Positions: 'level' = where along the bone (ref knee/ankle = joint line, prox_end/dist_end = bone ends, distal_mm = mm towards the foot; or diaphysis + frac 0..1). Angles: tilt_deg 0 = transverse; azimuth_deg 0 anterior, 90 medial, 180 posterior, 270 lateral. Prism outlines are drawn on the joint surface in (u, v): u -1 = lateral edge, +1 = medial edge; v -1 = posterior edge, +1 = anterior edge. Fragment sides: + = proximal side of a plane or spiral, or inside a prism.

Shaft-type values describe the DISTAL part relative to the proximal part: shortening_mm, lateral_mm, posterior_mm, varus_deg (negative = valgus), apex_anterior_deg (negative = apex posterior), external_rotation_deg. Fragment-type values: away_mm (straight away from the fracture site), proximal_mm, use_impaction (use the impaction stored with a depressed fragment). Shortening is reduced automatically until the bone ends no longer overlap.

sources.claim: heel height 40.8 mm at injury, 47.8 mm after fixation (Sanders 3 and 4)

calc_tuberosity.basis: Tuberosity moved laterally (5 mm, widening), into varus (7 deg) and turned with its back end up (4 deg, flatter Boehler angle); the loss of height shows as the depressed facet piece. Directions from the sources; sizes are teaching values within their ranges.

sources.ref: Guo 2021 (tongue type)

calc_tongue.basis: Tongue turned about its upper front edge: the back of the tongue goes up (Achilles pull) and the facet tips down (Essex-Lopresti). Size is a teaching value.

sources.ref: Sanders 1993
sources.claim: posterior facet pieces displaced (classification on coronal CT)

calc_joint_depression.basis: Joint piece pushed down into the body by the depth cut for it (6 mm) and turned with its front edge down. Sizes are teaching values.
